unqualified: production request billing and trace completeness
methodology: One local ARM64 run, pull first then push; paced persistent psql writes with concurrent capture/import/publication; two-second resource/progress sampling includes observer overhead. Application timing covers the BEGIN/INSERT/COMMIT round trip. Cross-database frontier observations are sequential, not atomic. RSS sums count shared pages repeatedly; PSS apportions shared pages. Cgroup peak is container lifetime, not interval peak; memory includes cache. Database size includes heap/catalog/index bytes, not only capture metadata. Object count is not request count. Timing includes final drain and observation. Publication transaction count uses fresh receipt xmin values in this short-lived fixture, not a durable public metric. No production acceptance threshold. MinIO S3 traces aggregate observed requests by private source/destination prefix and file kind, excluding witness object/list requests and retaining no request headers, object paths or bodies. Bucket-wide requests, including controller discovery, remain separate. Trace byte counts describe observed protocol traffic, not exact object sizes. This is observed traffic, not a production billing or trace-completeness guarantee. Destination PostgreSQL and its engine are sampled too; all_database_cpu_seconds sums the four database/engine containers, excluding object storage and host/controller CPU. Sampling overhead is included.
